name: geometrikks
description: GeoMetrikks tails your reverse proxy's access logs, looks up where every request came from with MaxMind GeoLite2, and shows the result on a live map and a traffic analytics dashboard. It reads nginx, Traefik JSON and Caddy JSON logs, detected per file. The only outbound traffic is the GeoLite2 download and a public-IP lookup for the map's home location, which you can turn off. Features: • Live map with heatmap and marker views, and routes that fly in as requests arrive • Overview and analytics for requests, bandwidth, latency, status mix, top URLs and user agents, plus a Top ASNs view of the networks your traffic comes from • Searchable access log history with filters and sorting, a live tail, and a debug view of the raw lines behind parse failures • CrowdSec integration: active bans next to the traffic that caused them, ban or unban IPs and ranges from the UI, and abuse reports for hosting providers • Password login, or OpenID Connect sign-in against Authelia, Authentik, Keycloak, Pocket ID or Google • Multi-source ingestion: tail several files from one instance, or run headless agents on other hosts that write into the same database • Batch import of rotated and archived logs • Application logs in the UI, plus a login log that fail2ban and CrowdSec can parse Requirements: • A TimescaleDB + PostGIS database. Install the companion "geometrikks-timescaledb" template from this repository first, or point the container at your own instance. • A free MaxMind GeoLite2 account (https://www.maxmind.com/en/geolite2/signup) for the GeoIP databases. • A free CARTO basemaps API key (https://carto.com/basemaps/apikey) for the map tiles. See the repository README for full setup steps.

paths.name: Access Logs
paths.description: Host directory holding your reverse proxy's access logs, mounted read-only. The default assumes SWAG. Point it at wherever nginx, Nginx Proxy Manager, Traefik or Caddy writes instead. The files must be readable by PUID:PGID. Whichever proxy you run, the container-side path stays /var/log/access, so that is what LOGPARSER_LOG_PATHS refers to.

paths.name: GeoIP Data
paths.description: Persistent storage for the downloaded MaxMind GeoLite2 City and ASN databases. The container fixes ownership of this folder to PUID:PGID on every start, so no manual chown is needed.

paths.name: App Logs
paths.description: Where GeoMetrikks writes its own logs: geometrikks.log (structured JSONL) and login.log (plain text, fail2ban/CrowdSec-friendly), plus their gzipped archives. Mounting this keeps logs across container recreation and lets host-side tools read login.log. Ownership is fixed to PUID:PGID on start.

ports.name: WebUI
ports.description: HTTP port for the GeoMetrikks web UI.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_LOG_PATHS
variables.description: Access log file(s) to tail, named as the container sees them under /var/log/access. Single path, or a JSON list ["/var/log/access/access.log", "/var/log/access/site2/access.log"] for several files.

variables.name: DB_HOST
variables.description: IP address of your TimescaleDB container, typically your Unraid server's IP if you installed the companion geometrikks-timescaledb template. Do not use localhost or 127.0.0.1, which is this container itself. The database container must be running and its port reachable from here.

variables.name: DB_PASSWORD
variables.description: Database password. Must match POSTGRES_PASSWORD in the geometrikks-timescaledb template.

variables.name: MAXMINDDB_USER_ID
variables.description: MaxMind account ID, used to download the GeoLite2 databases. Free account: https://www.maxmind.com/en/geolite2/signup

variables.name: MAXMINDDB_LICENSE_KEY
variables.description: MaxMind license key, used to download the GeoLite2 databases. Create it under your MaxMind account.

variables.name: MAP_CARTO_API_KEY
variables.description: CARTO basemaps API key, sent with every basemap request the browser makes. CARTO's terms require one per deployment and keyless tiles may stop working. Free at https://carto.com/basemaps/apikey. Not a secret: anyone who can open the map can see it.

variables.name: APP_ADMIN_USER
variables.description: Web UI login username.

variables.name: APP_ADMIN_PASSWORD
variables.description: Web UI login password. Leave it blank only if you set APP_AUTH_DISABLED=true or configured OIDC_* below; otherwise the container refuses to start. With OIDC configured, a password set here keeps the password form next to the provider button, so you can still log in when the provider is down.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_IGNORE_IPS
variables.description: IPs/CIDRs the parser drops entirely - no geo event, access log or debug row. Use it to keep your own WAN traffic through the reverse proxy out of the data(LAN traffic is never ingested), e.g. 88.99.77.66. Single value, comma-separated, or a JSON list. Empty (default): nothing is ignored.

variables.name: DB_PORT
variables.description: Database port.

variables.name: DB_USER
variables.description: Database user. Must match POSTGRES_USER in the geometrikks-timescaledb template.

variables.name: DB_DATABASE
variables.description: Database name. Must match POSTGRES_DB in the geometrikks-timescaledb template.

variables.name: PUID
variables.description: User ID the app runs as. The container starts as root only long enough to remap its internal user and fix ownership of the GeoIP and App Logs folders, then drops privileges. 99 is Unraid's 'nobody' - keep it so the appdata folders match the rest of your shares, and so nginx logs written by SWAG/NPM (which also default to 99:100) stay readable.

variables.name: PGID
variables.description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 is Unraid's 'users' group.

variables.name: LOG_LEVEL
variables.description: Application log verbosity (DEBUG, INFO, WARNING, ERROR).

variables.name: LOGPARSER_HOST_NAME
variables.description: Hostname label attached to ingested log events. A JSON list matched to LOGPARSER_LOG_PATHS by position labels each file separately, e.g. ["edge-01", "edge-02"], and the UI then filters them as separate sources.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_LOG_FORMATS
variables.description: Format of the file(s) above: auto (detected per file), geometrikks-json, nginx, traefik-json or caddy-json. One value covers every path, or give a JSON list matched to LOGPARSER_LOG_PATHS by position. Leave at auto unless detection gets it wrong.

variables.name: APP_SESSION_SECURE
variables.description: Mark the session cookie Secure so browsers only send it over HTTPS. Set true when you reach the UI through a TLS reverse proxy; leave false if you browse to http://server-ip:8000 directly, or you will not be able to log in. An https OIDC_REDIRECT_URI requires true, and the app will not start otherwise.

variables.name: APP_TRUSTED_PROXIES
variables.description: Reverse-proxy IPs/CIDRs allowed to supply X-Forwarded-For, e.g. 172.17.0.0/16 for Unraid's docker bridge. Single value, comma-separated, or a JSON list. Empty (default): forwarded headers are never trusted.

variables.name: APP_AUTH_DISABLED
variables.description: Set true ONLY if this container sits behind an authenticating reverse proxy (Authelia, Tailscale, etc). There is then no login and no session: anyone who can reach the container has full access. It cannot be combined with the OIDC_* settings below, and the app will not start if you set both.

variables.name: ANALYTICS_RAW_RETENTION_DAYS
variables.description: Days to keep raw geo_events and access_logs data.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_LAPI_URL
variables.description: CrowdSec Local API base URL, including http:// or https://, e.g. http://crowdsec:8080. Without the scheme the connection fails. Leave blank to disable CrowdSec integration.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_BOUNCER_API_KEY
variables.description: Bouncer API key (cscli bouncers add geometrikks) - grants read access to CrowdSec decisions.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_MACHINE_ID
variables.description: Machine ID (cscli machines add) - optional, enables ban/unban from the GeoMetrikks UI. Set it together with the machine password, or the app will not start.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_MACHINE_PASSWORD
variables.description: Machine password - optional, enables ban/unban from the GeoMetrikks UI. Set it together with the machine ID, or the app will not start.

variables.name: OIDC_ISSUER
variables.description: Issuer URL of your identity provider, e.g. https://auth.example.com. Leave blank to keep OIDC off. GeoMetrikks reads {issuer}/.well-known/openid-configuration and the token's iss claim must match this value exactly. Must be https unless the host is localhost. Filling in this plus the client id, secret and redirect URI puts a 'Sign in with ...' button on the login page.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_ID
variables.description: Client id of the confidential client you registered for GeoMetrikks at the provider. The authorization code flow with PKCE is used, so a public client will not work.

variables.name: OIDC_CLIENT_SECRET
variables.description: Client secret for that client.

variables.name: OIDC_REDIRECT_URI
variables.description: The exact callback URL registered at the provider: this container's public address plus /api/v1/auth/oidc/callback, e.g. https://geo.example.com/api/v1/auth/oidc/callback. It has to end in that path, and plain http is only accepted on localhost. With an https URL you also need APP_SESSION_SECURE=true.

variables.name: OIDC_ALLOWED_USERS
variables.description: Who may sign in, as verified email addresses or subject identifiers. Single value, comma-separated, or a JSON list. An email only matches when the provider marks it verified. At least one of OIDC_ALLOWED_USERS and OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS is required: without an allow list, everyone the provider authenticates would get in, which for Google means everyone.

variables.name: OIDC_ALLOWED_GROUPS
variables.description: Groups allowed to sign in; being in any one of them is enough. Same formats as OIDC_ALLOWED_USERS. The provider has to send the group claim, so keep the groups scope in OIDC_SCOPES.

variables.name: OIDC_SCOPES
variables.description: Space-separated scopes requested at login; openid is mandatory. Authelia works with the default. Google rejects the groups scope, and Authentik only sends groups if you add the mapping yourself, so use 'openid profile email' for those and allow people by email in OIDC_ALLOWED_USERS.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_DEFAULT_BAN_DURATION
variables.description: Default duration for manual bans (Go duration string).

variables.name: CROWDSEC_REQUEST_TIMEOUT
variables.description: LAPI request timeout in seconds.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_VERIFY_TLS
variables.description: Verify TLS when LAPI uses https.

variables.name: CROWDSEC_STREAM_POLL_INTERVAL
variables.description: Seconds between decision-stream polls feeding live ban/unban updates.

variables.name: OIDC_GROUPS_CLAIM
variables.description: Claim that carries group membership. It is read from the ID token and from the userinfo endpoint, so providers that only serve groups from userinfo (Authelia) need nothing extra.

variables.name: OIDC_PROVIDER_NAME
variables.description: Label on the login button: 'Sign in with {name}'.

variables.name: OIDC_LOGOUT_IDP
variables.description: On logout, also end the session at the provider. This only works when the provider's discovery document advertises an end_session_endpoint; Authelia 4.39 and Google do not, so leave it false there. Before enabling it, register {your app URL}/signed-out as the post-logout redirect URI at the provider. Logout always clears the GeoMetrikks session either way.

variables.name: OIDC_CA_BUNDLE
variables.description: PEM file holding the CA that signed your provider's certificate, for a provider behind an internal CA. Give the path as the container sees it and add a path mapping for the file yourself, e.g. host /mnt/user/appdata/geometrikks/certs/ca.pem to container /app/certs/ca.pem, readable by PUID:PGID. The app refuses to start when the file is missing. There is no switch to turn certificate verification off.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_ENABLED
variables.description: Tail and ingest the access logs. Set false for an instance that only serves the UI over data another instance writes.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_POLL_INTERVAL
variables.description: Interval in seconds to poll the log file for new entries. Lower it (1.0 is the app default) for a snappier live map, at the cost of more wakeups.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_BATCH_SIZE
variables.description: Max records before a forced commit.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_COMMIT_INTERVAL
variables.description: Max time interval in seconds between database commits.

variables.name: LOGPARSER_STORE_DEBUG_LINES
variables.description: Store all raw log lines in the debug table, not just malformed ones.

variables.name: GEOIP_ASN_ENABLED
variables.description: Download the GeoLite2 ASN database alongside the City one and record the network and organization behind each request. This is what fills the Top ASNs view. Uses the same MaxMind credentials; without them the app ingests without ASN data.

variables.name: GEOIP_REFRESH_DAYS
variables.description: Re-download the GeoLite2 databases when older than this many days.

variables.name: GEOIP_LOCALES
variables.description: JSON list of GeoIP locales to use.

variables.name: MAP_DEFAULT_VIEW
variables.description: Where the map opens, as latitude,longitude or latitude,longitude,zoom (zoom 0-22, default 3), e.g. 71.129982,27.653369,15. Unset: the map opens on your site homes, or the whole world when there are none.

variables.name: MAP_AUTO_DETECT_HOME
variables.description: Resolve the server's public IP at startup and geolocate it when home coordinates are unset.

variables.name: MAP_PUBLIC_IP_URL
variables.description: JSON endpoint used for public-IP discovery; response must contain an 'ip' field.

variables.name: MAP_HOME_REFRESH_HOURS
variables.description: Hours between re-detections of this instance's own public IP and its map home location.

variables.name: MAP_HOME_LOCATIONS
variables.description: Per-hostname home overrides as a JSON object of latitude/longitude pairs, e.g. {"edge-01": [59.91, 10.75]}. Use it for a source whose public IP geolocates wrong (CGNAT, VPN) or for hostnames in logs shipped from another machine. An override beats auto-detection; delete the entry and its row goes at the next start.

variables.name: ANALYTICS_DEBUG_RETENTION_DAYS
variables.description: Days to keep access_log_debug data.

variables.name: ANALYTICS_HOURLY_RETENTION_DAYS
variables.description: Days to keep hourly continuous aggregate data.

variables.name: ANALYTICS_CAGG_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MINUTES
variables.description: Minutes between continuous aggregate refreshes.

variables.name: ANALYTICS_COMPRESSION_AFTER_DAYS
variables.description: Days after which to compress hypertable chunks.

variables.name: SCHEDULER_ENABLED
variables.description: Enable scheduled background tasks.

variables.name: LOG_MAIN_MAX_BYTES
variables.description: Rotate the main JSONL log (geometrikks.log) when it exceeds this size in bytes. Default 10 MiB.

variables.name: LOG_MAIN_BACKUP_COUNT
variables.description: Number of gzipped main-log archives to keep.

variables.name: LOG_LOGIN_MAX_BYTES
variables.description: Rotate the login log (login.log) when it exceeds this size in bytes. Default 10 MiB.

variables.name: LOG_LOGIN_BACKUP_COUNT
variables.description: Number of gzipped login-log archives to keep.

variables.name: DB_STARTUP_WAIT_SECONDS
variables.description: How long startup waits for the database before serving in degraded mode. 0 probes once. The app keeps retrying in the background and recovers on its own when the database answers.

variables.name: APP_MODE
variables.description: full runs everything: web UI, API, migrations, scheduler, CrowdSec and ingestion. agent is headless. It tails, geolocates and writes into a shared database and serves only /health and /health/ready, so the WebUI port and the admin login do nothing. Set agent only on an extra copy of this container that feeds a full instance elsewhere, and give it the same image tag as that instance.

variables.name: APP_PROXY_ADVISORY
variables.description: Warn on Settings > Status when recent traffic for a tailed file comes from CDN or private addresses, which means the proxy is logging the hop in front of it rather than the visitor. Set false when that traffic mix is deliberate, such as Tailscale-only access or a CDN you front on purpose.
